partners.mechanism_chain: F13B (HGNC:3758) —DISRUPTS→ Platelet aggregation (GO:0007550); Platelet aggregation (GO:0007550) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001892); ITGA2B (HGNC:6075) —BINDS→ Platelet aggregation (GO:0007550); Platelet aggregation (GO:0007550) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal bleeding (HP:00114169); F13B (HGNC:3758) —LEADS_TO→ Fibrinogenemia (HP:0030177). Loss-of-function mutations in F13B disrupt the function of coagulation factor XIII B subunit, which is essential for stabilizing fibrin clots and normal platelet aggregation. This disruption leads to thrombocytopenia and abnormal bleeding. While ITGA2B is also implicated in platelet function, F13B's role in stabilizing the platelet plug and its relation to fibrinogen suggests a convergence point in platelet aggregation pathways. Fetomaternal alloimmune thrombocytopenia B is characterized by maternal antibodies against fetal platelet antigens, often involving ITGA2B, leading to fetal thrombocytopenia. A shared mechanism could involve F13B's role in clot stabilization and platelet function, potentially impacting fetal platelet survival or maternal immune response indirectly.
